title: Quant Spectra: throughput-fidelity sweep harness for long-tail prompts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: build a repeatable, CI-friendly harness ("Quant Spectra") that sweeps FP16 / INT8 / INT4 quantization configurations across a curated long-tail prompt corpus and realistic arrival patterns to produce: tokens/sec, p95 and p99 latencies, tail throughput under burst, and quality deltas (exact-match / semantic-similarity / safety flags).

Why: prior quantization sweeps focused on head workloads and short prompts. Customer workloads show large quality regressions on long-tail prompts that only surface at scale or under burst. We need an automated way to detect regressions and quantify the throughput/fidelity trade space so operators can choose safe quant bins for Dedicated and Private deploys.

Scope:
- Implement harness that runs controlled load tests with: constant-rate, Poisson burst, and realistic playback (from production traces) arrival patterns.
- Sweep quant configs: FP16 (baseline), per-layer INT8, group-wise INT8, hybrid INT8/FP16, and aggressive INT4 variants (two tooling presets: conserv-4 and aggressive-4).
- Collect: tokens/sec, p95, p99, p50, request success rate, memory footprint per model, KV cache hit/miss breakdown, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, paired human-quality proxies via embed-similarity delta and safety label rate).
- Regression detection: compute rolling baseline from FP16 run, flag quality drop > 3% absolute on key metrics OR latency p95 regression > 25% OR tokens/sec drop > 30% vs baseline.
- Integrations: output JSON artifacts for dashboards, add automatic PR comment with run summary when harness run in CI, and wire into canary rollout jobs for Dedicated customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness runs end-to-end in CI and stores artifacts in s3://redwood-bench/quant-spectra/<date>/<run-id>.json (see artifact schema in Confluence).
- Regression detector produces human-readable summary and metric diffs and files an ENG ticket when thresholds are crossed.
- Dashboard panels for throughput vs quality, quant-variant comparison heatmap, and per-prompt long-tail failure list are present in Grafana runtime-perf dashboard.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing loadbench-v2 harness for arrival shaping but add a "quality-check" stage that sends responses to the evaluation harness (quant-eval) which runs emb-sim and heuristic safety checks.
- Leverage kernel-selection logs (via runtime tracing) to correlate kernel choices with latency spikes.
- For INT4 runs, include repeated seeds and 3 independent runs per config to capture instability.

Risks and mitigation:
- Long-run cost: schedule heavy sweeps on off-peak dedicated pools and use sampling of long-tail prompts to bound cost.
- Noise in quality metrics: add automated noise floor estimation and require >95% CI on deltas before alerting.

Deliverables:
- quant-spectra harness in repositories/benchmarks (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/142)
